lead.title: Mistral ships Voxtral 3: a voice agent SDK with self-deployable speech models in 50+ languages
lead.summary: Mistral announced Voxtral 3, a voice agent SDK plus speech models for real-time transcription and voice generation across more than 50 languages. Its Voxtral Small Transcribe 3 model is state-of-the-art in multilingual transcription with diarization and context-biasing, and a 4B Mini variant targets smaller hardware. Models are available via Mistral's EU-hosted API or for self-deployment, putting frontier-grade voice pipelines inside local stacks.

top_stories.title: Ornith-1.5-122B: MIT-licensed 122B MoE built for single-GPU serving
top_stories.summary: Ornith AI released a 122B (256-expert, top-8) MIT-licensed MoE with 262K context and native vision — vendor-reported 84.5 SWE-bench Verified, with official FP8, NVFP4, GGUF and MLX builds targeting a single 80GB GPU or a 64GB Mac, and day-one support in Ollama, vLLM and llama.cpp.

top_stories.title: Meta's Muse Glimmer 30B: Apache-2.0 on-device agentic model with 4-bit weights and a speculator head
top_stories.summary: Meta Superintelligence Labs open-sourced a 30B multimodal causal LM purpose-built for always-on local agents on consumer hardware — multi-step reasoning, tool use and failure recovery in one model, with official ~4-bit quants and a DFlash speculative-decoding head.

top_stories.title: TorchTPU goes open source — native PyTorch on TPUs lands in the Hugging Face stack
top_stories.summary: Hugging Face and Google announced TorchTPU, a native PyTorch backend that makes TPU 'just another device' — no torch_xla porting, no JAX. Transformers, Diffusers and Kernels run natively on TPU, giving local-AI builders a third hardware path alongside CUDA and Metal.

top_stories.title: DeepSeek open-sources DeepInfer, an inference framework with Nvidia and Ascend support
top_stories.summary: DeepSeek released DeepInfer plus a companion recipe repo; the accelerator platform is selected with a single environment variable ('nvidia' or 'ascend'). The community flagged the explicit Ascend support as lowering the barrier to running DeepSeek models at scale independent of Nvidia hardware.

items.title: Don't skip the baseline: many MoE expert-skipping methods lose to a simple calibrated baseline
items.summary: A controlled comparison finds dynamic expert-skipping methods for MoE models are evaluated under inconsistent calibration regimes — benchmarked against one calibrated baseline, several proposed mechanisms fail to beat it while reducing active parameters per token.

items.title: PACT: NVFP4 data-flow LoRA fine-tuning on consumer GPUs
items.summary: A LoRA fine-tuning system that accelerates frozen projections with native NVFP4 GEMMs on consumer GPUs, cutting quantization/dequantization overhead and reusing quantized RMSNorm activations to shrink activation memory.

items.title: The KV-Surgeon: compensation-aware offline KV-cache compaction
items.summary: An offline KV-cache compaction method that accounts for softmax renormalization coupling between cache entries when deciding what to delete, improving reuse of a compacted cache for repeated queries over a fixed context.

items.title: LOOP: recovery-aligned iterative layer pruning via on-policy distillation
items.summary: Replaces one-shot layer pruning with recovery-aligned iterative pruning guided by on-policy distillation, preserving reasoning capability while shrinking the model for standard hardware.

items.title: ACE-Compression: measuring which abilities survive quantization and pruning
items.summary: An evaluation framework that goes beyond retained task scores to measure which underlying abilities survive or collapse under LLM compression, exposing failures standard benchmarks hide.

items.title: Reflection Beam 501B-A23B: US lab's first open-weight model, Apache 2.0, trending on the Hub
items.summary: Reflection AI's Beam (501B total / 23B active sparse MoE) went Apache 2.0 on Hugging Face and is still trending — built for coding, reasoning and long-horizon agentic work, with explicit permission for distillation, fine-tuning and quantization; a 293.7GB NVFP4 variant targets self-hosters.

items.title: r/LocalLLaMA debate: '72 hours, four big open-weights drops — only NVIDIA's fits in 24GB'
items.summary: A hot thread plotted four releases (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, Muse Spark Open 816B, Reflection Beam 501B, Nemotron 3.5 Bolt) against a 24GB VRAM line and argued open weights no longer means runnable locally — the only one that fit came from NVIDIA.

items.title: BigMoeOnEdge: a llama.cpp layer that streams frontier-size MoE models on phones and laptops
items.summary: An open-source layer on top of stock llama.cpp that runs MoE models larger than available RAM by streaming experts from disk, losslessly, on phones and laptops.

items.title: ane-fieldfare: reverse-engineered Apple Neural Engine runs Gemma 4 26B at ~100 tok/s
items.summary: A project reverse-engineering Apple's Neural Engine to run Gemma 4 26B-A4B at roughly 100 tokens per second, bypassing the official Core ML path.

items.title: Harness Studio: open-source desktop coding agent for any model
items.summary: An open-source desktop coding agent app for macOS and Linux that works with any model, built on the DeepSeek Harness.

items.title: Melra: local MCP runtime that gates risky AI-agent tool calls on approval
items.summary: An open-source local MCP runtime that inspects agent tool calls, pauses ambiguous or risky writes for human approval instead of blindly retrying, and verifies results.

items.title: MCP Census: live change feed tracking 48,797 MCP servers
items.summary: A live change feed monitoring nearly 49,000 MCP servers, surfacing updates and changes across the MCP ecosystem.

items.title: ASUS reveals UGen Arc Pro B70 with 32GB ECC GDDR6 for local AI inference
items.summary: ASUS published product info for its first Intel Arc-branded inference card — Xe2 BMG-G31, 32GB ECC GDDR6 at 608 GB/s, up to 367 INT8 TOPS — explicitly listing Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM, PyTorch and OpenVINO support; four cards pool to 128GB of ECC VRAM.

items.title: Perplexity Computer now runs fully local on Apple Silicon Macs, with a 36GB RAM catch
items.summary: Perplexity launched a fully local mode of its Computer agent for Pro, Max and Enterprise subscribers, running Qwen 3.6 and its PPLX Pro model entirely on Apple Silicon — but the recommended 36GB+ memory floor makes an M5 Max Mac Studio or a 48-64GB M5 Pro Mac mini the practical minimum.

items.title: ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent reportedly order 3 million Nvidia RTX Pro 5500 GPUs
items.summary: Chinese tech giants reportedly placed orders for over 3 million RTX Pro 5500 workstation cards (84GB GDDR7) worth more than $35 billion; Nvidia has reportedly warned only 5-10% can be fulfilled, tightening availability of the high-VRAM cards local-AI users also target.
